title: Loop Control: break, continue, and Flags
objective: Exit or skip parts of a loop with break and continue, and track loop state with a flag variable.

sourceAlignment.title: Python Crash Course, 3rd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Eric Matthes
sourceAlignment.chapterTitle: Using break to Exit a Loop; Using continue in a Loop; Using a Flag
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: break immediately exits the nearest loop, even if its condition is still True. Execution jumps straight to the first line after the loop — nothing else in the loop body runs for that pass or any future one.

continue skips the rest of the current pass and jumps back to re-check the loop's condition, without exiting the loop entirely. Any code in the loop body written after continue is skipped for that pass only.

A flag is a Boolean variable you use to track whether a loop should keep running, especially when the stopping condition depends on several different things. Starting a flag as True and setting it to False when it's time to stop keeps a while loop's condition simple, like while is_running:.
explanation.rule: break exits a loop completely; continue skips to the next pass without exiting.

examples.title: Skipping and Stopping
examples.note: 3 is skipped by continue; the loop stops entirely once count reaches 6, so 6 and beyond never print.

checks.question: Inside a while loop, which statement skips the rest of the current pass but keeps the loop running afterward?

feedback.correct: Correct — continue skips to the next pass; break would stop the loop entirely.
feedback.incorrect: That's break's job (or a different statement entirely). continue skips just the current pass.

assignment.title: Skip and Stop
assignment.brief: Write count_to(limit) using a while loop that prints numbers from 1 up to limit, skipping any multiple of 3 with continue, and stopping immediately (with break) once it would print a number greater than or equal to limit.
requirements: Use a while loop with continue to skip multiples of 3.
Use break to stop once the counter reaches limit.
assignment.starterCode:
def count_to(limit):
    # Print 1..limit, skipping multiples of 3, stopping at limit.
    pass

count_to(7)
assignment.testHarness:
# ---- Code Forge validation ----
import io, contextlib
_cf_buf = io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(_cf_buf):
    count_to(7)
_cf_result = _cf_buf.getvalue()
print("__CF_TEST_OUTPUT__")
print(repr(_cf_result))

hints: You can loop with while True: and use break to stop manually.
Increment your counter first, then check if it's over the limit — break if so.
Check count % 3 == 0 to detect multiples of 3, and continue past them.
For limit=7, the multiples of 3 skipped are 3 and 6; the rest print.
